userStories.title: Verification executor stall lifecycle
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Stop stalled verification through bounded timeout cleanup.
**Motivation** — Verification tests use `verification/executor.ts:executeWithTimeout`, whose `Response.text()` collectors reveal output only after closure.
**Approach** — Wire the observer into `executeWithTimeout`: concurrent incremental collectors, the single terminal latch, detector evidence on the raw result and the existing process-group cleanup. Preserve trust-before-spawn, output exposure and every ordering guarantee.
Use concurrent incremental collectors in executeWithTimeout, starting both reads before waiting on exit; quality engine wiring belongs to US-005. The verification collector needs to expose the text accumulated so far instead of depending on `Response.text()` finishing. The quality collector already provides a useful precedent. Feed bytes to the monitor as they arrive while retaining original output text; detector normalization must not rewrite the captured stream.
A single terminal latch arbitrates normal leader exit, wall timeout, repetition and silence. The first event observed while the invocation is live wins. If leader exit has already been observed, queued detector/deadline callbacks and output drained afterwards cannot change that exit into a timeout. If a detector wins first, a subsequent exit 0 cannot turn the interrupted run into a pass. On an exact scheduling tie, callback observation order decides; tests drive each ordering rather than asserting an OS-level simultaneity guarantee.
An early stop enters the same cleanup lane as a wall timeout: detached process group, SIGTERM, bounded grace, group liveness probe, SIGKILL for remaining members even when the leader exited, no single-pid fallback after leader exit, bounded concurrent stream drains. Each invocation starts at most one termination sequence. Clear all wall/silence/grace/drain timers, disable detector callbacks on settlement, and cancel readers best-effort when drain deadlines expire. A stream error keeps bytes already collected and leaves existing exit/error policy intact; it is not itself repetition or silence.
**Scope** — In: executor.ts, TestExecutionResult and lifecycle tests. Out: US-004 lists/ops, US-005 quality, US-007/008 gate injection. Refactoring all command runners into one engine, changing shell/trust/sandbox behavior, platform expansion beyond the current process-group support, or dependency/version changes.
**Interface** — `executeWithTimeout(command, timeoutSeconds, env?, options?)` retains its call shape with optional `options.stallDetection`. Raw verification early stops return `success:false`, `timeout:true`, `killed:true`, `childProcessesKilled:true`, `countsTowardEscalation:false`, plus `stopReason`. Their `error` begins `EXECUTION_STALLED:` and identifies repeated output (stream/count/threshold) or configured silence, rather than falsely saying the wall timeout elapsed.

userStories.title: Verification lists, interruption routing and test operations
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry independent detector evidence through verification lists and timeout routing in test operations.
**Motivation** — Both otherwise wait for their wall-clock limit when a command endlessly repeats a line.
**Approach** — Preserve raw first-failure list aggregation while carrying independent interruption evidence, and route it in `verifyScopedOp` and `fullSuiteGateOp`: no zero-tests rerun, the interruption route, and the existing accept-on-timeout contract with the reason on both forms.
A verification command list keeps its historical raw aggregation, and interruption evidence is carried independently so a consumer cannot mistake a mixed list for an ordinary code failure:
`status`, `exitCode` and `error` remain the first unsuccessful entry's values. `success` remains "every entry succeeded". `countsTowardEscalation` remains the any-entry `some`. `output`, `passCount` and `failCount` are unchanged.
The list's `stopReason` is the first detector reason in command order, and is absent when no entry was stopped. Its presence — not the aggregate `status` — is the interruption evidence.
`verifyScopedOp` treats `status === "TIMEOUT" || stopReason !== undefined` as interrupted: it never starts the zero-tests full-suite rerun, and it returns `status:"timeout"` with the reason instead of a code-failure verdict. `fullSuiteGateOp` derives its internal `timedOut` from the same predicate, so the existing `acceptOnTimeout` translation still decides `passed-on-timeout` versus `timeout` — with the reason on both forms, and `runWorkflowSuiteGate` still reporting `passed-on-timeout` as red and timed out. Lists with no stopped entry keep today's behaviour exactly; ordinary historical list semantics are not rewritten.
**Scope** — In: verification/types.ts and runners.ts, verify-scoped.ts, full-suite-gate.ts and workflow/gates.ts suite wrapper. Out: raw executor lifecycle (US-003), mechanical story checks (US-008), bootstrap setup. Pass parsed package/gate-context policy to every test run including legitimate fallback. Preserve existing TIMEOUT/acceptOnTimeout tests while extending shapes. Use controlled injected results for both mixed-list orders and real operation entry points.
**Interface** — `VerificationGateOptions` gains optional `stallDetection`; `VerificationResult`, `VerifyScopedOutput` and `FullSuiteGateOutput` gain optional `stopReason`. `[ordinary failure, detector stop]` keeps `TEST_FAILURE`; `[detector stop, ordinary failure]` keeps `TIMEOUT`; both route interruption. Existing statuses and escalation semantics are retained.

userStories.title: Quality runner stall lifecycle and bounded settlement
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Interrupt stalled quality commands and bound settlement even when child exit never arrives.
**Motivation** — Mechanical checks and repository gates use `quality/runner.ts:runQualityCommand`, which already collects streams incrementally.
**Approach** — Extend the quality runner's existing incremental collectors with the same observer and single-stop latch, replace the direct exit await with the bounded terminal race, and carry the reason through single-command results without changing output exposure or cleanup behavior.
The quality runner adopts the executor's shape: one terminal race between the child exit and the first stop signal (wall, repetition or silence), a post-signal wait bounded by the configured grace period, then the existing bounded drains, then the stopped result — every armed timer cleared and stalled readers cancelled best-effort. A never-settling `proc.exited` with pending pipes must still produce the stopped result after those bounds. Process-group escalation and the no-bare-pid rule after an observed leader exit are unchanged.
A rejected `proc.exited` keeps today's floating `.catch(() => {})`: it is not stall evidence, it does not reclassify a result, and repairing exit-rejection handling is explicitly out of this feature's scope (see Out of Scope).
Keep existing output exposure: verification returns collected stdout then stderr; successful quality commands preserve the existing combined output; stopped quality harness commands expose only the diagnostic notice, while `origin:"agent-tool"` retains its bounded 4,000-character, line-boundary tail. Merely adding a stop reason must not enable heuristic stopping for agent-tool calls. Existing environment stripping, agent-output markers, NO_COLOR behavior, shell quoting, trusted-cwd checks, and actual working directories are unchanged. New structured logging carries reason/threshold/stream/count, not a copy of the repeated line or raw output.
**Scope** — In: quality/runner.ts options/results/collectors/latch/cleanup. Out: US-006 aggregation, US-007/008 gate wiring. Repairing or reclassifying a rejected child-exit promise: this feature keeps today's floating catch and defines no new result policy for that error class. Preserve trust-before-monitor/spawn, both terminal observation orders, one SIGTERM/grace/probe/SIGKILL lane and best-effort bounded drains. Use fake clocks and controlled streams. runner.test.ts env/argv cases stay green unedited; only runner-drain.test.ts and runner-timeout-kill.test.ts gain bounded-settle changes preserving prior lifecycle invariants.
**Interface** — Optional `QualityCommandOptions.stallDetection` and `QualityCommandResult.stopReason`. Raw quality early stops return `success:false`, `timedOut:true`, `exitCode:-1`, plus `stopReason`. Quality output begins `[nax] <commandName> stopped early: repeated-output ...` or `[nax] <commandName> stopped early: silence ...`. Absent low-level policy creates no monitor.

userStories.title: Gate policy carrier, gate records and e2e setup
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry resolved trusted stall policy through repository gate descriptions, setup and records.
**Motivation** — Both otherwise wait for their wall-clock limit when a command endlessly repeats a line.
**Approach** — Resolve the policy onto every gate description, include it in overlay run identity, apply the leaf default to a policy-less gate, classify a stopped run as timed-out, copy its reason to the record, and pass the e2e gate's policy to its setup.
For repository gates, root-command precedence by key and current ordering stay intact. Overlay gates use field-wise root+overlay policy. Include the resolved policy in overlay run identity so otherwise identical command/setup runs with different policies are not silently deduplicated; identical resolved policies still dedupe as they do today. `GateCommand` is the policy carrier so bot worktree remapping need not reload configuration.
`resolveStallDetection` is not a decorative export: completing a sparse or absent policy is a production step reached from `runQualityGates`, so `_qualityGateDeps` (`run`, `loadConfig`, `loadPackageOverride`) gains a `resolveStallDetection` entry and the finish gate calls it through that seam for every gate before the quality runner runs, and `resolveGateCommands` calls it for the root policy and for the field-wise merged overlay policy it attaches. The deps entry is a plain delegation to the leaf function, the same shape as `run`; it exists so the resolution is observable at the production entry instead of being re-implemented inline.
**Scope** — In: finish/gates/quality.ts carrier/default/dedupe/records and e2e setup. Out: bot projection/CLI reporting (US-008), quality engine/list implementation (US-005/006). Capture the shared resolver with sparse input through real runRepoGates, then capture completed policy at _qualityGateDeps.run; final-value-only tests do not pin delegation. Existing exact gate-object tests may gain policy only: finish gates-quality/gates-quality-e2e, workflow repo-gates and integration runtime/package-profile-registry. Preserve precedence/order/root key identity, cwd, setup inheritance and later-gate execution.
**Interface** — GateCommand gains optional `stallDetection`; GateRunRecord gains optional `stopReason`. A manually constructed `GateCommand` without the optional field gets `DEFAULT_GATE_STALL_POLICY` at `runQualityGates`, not a new literal default in the engine. `runQualityGates` classifies early stops as timed-out before considering exit -1; existing caller repair/advisor routing is not broadened.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Wire harness gate entry points to policy and expose early-stop evidence without losing trust or provenance.
**Motivation** — Both otherwise wait for their wall-clock limit when a command endlessly repeats a line.
**Approach** — Wire mechanical story/review checks, setup verification and trusted bot gate projections to the resolved policy, carry early-stop evidence into gate records and the workflow gate-timeout route, and expose it through `nax gates run`. Preserve provenance, command order and bot snapshot trust. Every scoped-lint arm the design names — degraded, template, derived and full-lint — carries the policy, and the derived arm is pinned at command execution rather than only at the helper call.
In `runReview`, the policy crosses the injected `_scopedLintDeps.runLintCommand` helper boundary, so the helper signature carries it and every degraded, template, derived and full-lint path passes the same value. No story, projectDir, storyGitRef or scope is threaded into the production `runReview` adapter by this change. `_scopedLintDeps` additionally gains a `runQualityCommand` entry that the module's `runLintCommand` delegates to — the same plain-delegation shape as `_qualityGateDeps.run` — so a test can keep the real helper and capture the policy arriving at command execution for the derived arm, which is a distinct call site from the template and full-lint arms and is otherwise unpinned.
For instruction/detection-derived bot checks, attach the trusted resolver input's configured policy (schema defaults if unset), not LLM-extracted thresholds. `BotCheck.stallDetection` stays optional so hand-built check literals remain valid; an absent value falls back to `DEFAULT_GATE_STALL_POLICY` at the quality gate runner.
**Scope** — In: lint/typecheck ops, workflow gates, review runner/scoped lint, setup-verify, bot checks/fix/baseline projections and CLI gates report. Out: US-003–007 engine/carrier work. Applying stall policy to installation/pre-run/bootstrap steps, run-start baseline capture, native agent tools, ACP-owned tools, hooks, git processes, remote CI jobs/waits or plugin-owned subprocesses. Preserve authorized regression assertions (analysis). Use production entry points, injected streams/fake clocks and LLM doubles; keep policy mappings real.

GateReportEntry gains only optional `stopReason`, not cwd/raw output; passed outputTail stays absent. `nax gates run` keeps exit 0 for all gates passed, 2 for an unsuccessful/empty gate run, 1 for usage/trust/execution setup errors. `--json` writes one document to stdout. **Goal** — Remove consumer-invented branch work and persist unresolved verdict mismatch independently.
**Motivation** — These become `B` findings, consume fix rounds and inflate branch-found/fixed counts even though the reviewer named no defect.
**Approach** — Stop synthesizing verdict-floor work in `withQualityFloor`/`branchReviewStep`, derive mismatch kinds from the verdict itself, persist `reviewMismatch` through the feature machine, and keep every real fix path and finding count intact. userStories.title: Bounded clarification and coverage retry composition
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Compose one branch mismatch clarification with independent invocation-scoped JSON and coverage budgets.
**Motivation** — The honest alternative is to ask the reviewer once, then retain an explicit uncertainty reason that keeps the PR draft.
**Approach** — Composition: `makeCoverageRetryStrategy` wraps `makeMismatchClarificationStrategy`, which wraps the existing shape strategy. Each wrapper consults its inner strategy first, so shape repair, then clarification, then coverage is the effect of the nesting rather than a second priority table. Each wrapper subtracts the prompts it issued from the attempt number it passes inward, so the shape allowance stays one turn while clarification and coverage prompts are interleaved; the clarification wrapper owns one `clarified` latch and sets it when it issues, and the coverage wrapper records the attempt at which it last issued so a reply counts as a coverage response only when it answers that prompt. Because the shape strategy decides from the attempt number it is handed and holds no spent latch of its own, the clarification wrapper also owns an invocation-local count of shape-repair prompts already issued and adds it to the attempt it passes inward: a repair spent in one hop is therefore not reissued when a manager-owned fallback hop restarts the loop at 0. All of these counters live on the strategy instance, which `callOp` resolves once per invocation; the wrappers carry no other state and never see raw bytes or config.
A parseable mismatch gets at most one clarification turn for the entire invocation (both kinds together). Reuse the existing per-kind sentences; require the complete branch-review object, preserving findings, coverage evidence and minor triage, and ask to name the defect/failed AC or correct the verdict. This is read-only reviewer work, not a fix instruction.
On persistent mismatch, keep the last parseable verdict and mismatch; do not return null solely because it is inconsistent. If the clarification is malformed, the remaining shape allowance may repair it; once exhausted, retain the last parseable verdict, including real findings, rather than certifying it clean.
**Scope** — In: wrapper/resolver/builders/seams. Out: US-013 delivery, US-011 parser, US-010 readiness. userStories.title: Opt-in last-parseable dispatch handoff
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Deliver recorded plain-record retry fallback before post-parse hooks only for opted-in null parses.
**Motivation** — The honest alternative is to ask the reviewer once, then retain an explicit uncertainty reason that keeps the PR draft.
**Approach** — The opt-in branch validates with a new strict predicate, `isPlainRecord(value)`: `typeof value === "object"`, not null, not an array, and its prototype is either `Object.prototype` or `null`. This is deliberately **not** the check the existing throwing path uses — `validatedFallbackRecord` rejects only non-objects and null, so arrays and class instances pass it; the two predicates are separate and this feature does not claim the legacy one validates plain records.
When set, `op.parse` returns null/undefined and `retryState.retryFallback` satisfies `isPlainRecord`, that object is the parse result.
A `retryState.retryFallback` that is `undefined` or `null` counts as no fallback: the null parse result stands, so "no parseable reply" keeps today's skipped-review outcome and nothing is substituted.
A `retryState.retryFallback` that is present but fails `isPlainRecord` (array, class instance, function, string, number, boolean) raises the existing `CALL_OP_INVALID_FALLBACK` error naming the observed value, before `runPostParse`, so neither `verify` nor `recover` runs and no malformed verdict reaches the branch step.
The post-parse hooks keep their existing meaning for a substituted value: `verify` is called with the fallback object as the parsed value it observes, and `recover` runs only when `verify` returns null — exactly the split `runPostParse` implements today. Substituting the fallback must therefore happen before `runPostParse`, not by returning the fallback around it.
Operations without the flag keep today's behaviour exactly, including `validatedFallbackRecord`'s broader object check on the throwing path; `workflowBranchReviewOp` is the only op that sets it.
**Scope** — In: RunOperation flag, module-private predicate/null-parse handoff in call-dispatch-run.ts, sole branch-op opt-in and delivered wrapper outcomes. Out: retry composition/prompts/seam counts (US-012), global fallback precedence changes. Ensure strict validation errors cannot be swallowed by the legacy parse-failure ladder. Drive all handoff/hook/strict-class assertions through real callOp, not strategy-only/predicate tests.
**Interface** — `RunOperation.preferRetryFallbackOnNullParse?: true`; `isPlainRecord` lives privately in operations/call-dispatch-run.ts. Historical operations without the flag retain null-parse and throwing-path behavior unchanged.
